subject: FastRetail checkout: intermittent tail-latency spikes impacting checkout flow
messages:
From: FastRetail Support <support@fastretail.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout errors and stalls - seeing p99 spikes

Hi Olga,

We're seeing intermittent tail latency spikes in the checkout flow that began around 08:50 UTC. Our merchants are reporting timeouts during payment tokenization; some checkouts are failing client-side. Quick metrics from our side: p95 ~ 300ms, p99 jumping to 8-12s during spikes, error rate rose to ~1.8% (normally 0.02%), and aggregated throughput dropped by ~20% for the affected route.

Attaching a screenshot of our dashboard and a short trace. Can your team confirm whether this is on the Redwood API side or something in our integration? We did not deploy anything new.

Attachment: latency_screenshot.png, quick_trace.txt

—Mike
Mike Donovan
Senior SRE, FastRetail
mike.donovan@fastretail.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Donovan <mike.donovan@fastretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout errors and stalls - seeing p99 spikes

Thanks Mike — sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating this to infra and SRE to investigate immediately.

Plan:
- Marcus/Marissa/Dylan, can you pull the tenant routing logs and the model-variant metrics for FastRetail (tenant id: FR-221)? Look for concurrency cap saturations, KV cache miss rate, and any sustained micro-batching increases around 08:45–09:30 UTC.
- I'll set up a brief customer call in the next 30 minutes and keep them informed.

I'll follow up with a mitigation path within 20–30 minutes.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout errors and stalls - seeing p99 spikes

Quick findings: we've correlated FastRetail's error windows with sustained queuing on our serving fleet for model-variant xgen-v2-quant (seq len defaults). Observations:
- Concurrency caps for the tenant were at the configured hard limit (12) for several minutes during the spike window.
- Request batching increased (batch size rose ~3x) leading to longer pipeline times under bursty traffic.
- KV cache miss fraction for that variant spiked ~6x, suggesting cold cache behavior following a prior eviction.
- We also saw a small increase in tokenization errors (0.6% -> 1.1%) which correlates with the failing client-side timeouts.

Attachments: mrtg_logs.zip (request traces, scheduler counters snapshot)

Immediate mitigations we can apply now (ordered):
1) Increase concurrency cap for FR-221 from 12 -> 24 for 30 minutes (fastest, low code change).
2) Force route FastRetail traffic to xgen-v2-fp16-fallback variant (wider memory but lower batch latency) while we warm caches.
3) Reduce adaptive batching window for the tenant to prioritize latency over throughput.

If you want, I can roll #1 now. Note: raising per-tenant concurrency can impact co-tenants on that pool unless we move FR to a dedicated slot; monitor required.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Checkout errors and stalls - seeing p99 spikes

I support Marcus' mitigation plan. Quick operational notes:
- I can temporarily raise the concurrency cap for FR-221 to 24 for a 1-hour window from the control plane. That should immediately reduce queueing and p99.
- We'll instrument a traffic-shed watch to rollback automatically if we see adverse tail effects for other customers (we'll use a +2% global p99 threshold).
- I'll also throttle batch-aggregation for this tenant to use a 40ms window (default 120ms) to lower per-request latency.

I'll need a go-ahead from Olga (customer comms) and Evelyn (exec visibility/approval for cross-tenant risk).

Marissa

SRE Lead, Production Reliability

Subject: Re: Checkout errors and stalls - seeing p99 spikes

Mike — quick update from our side: we see the same tail spikes on our telemetry and have identified a likely serving-side backpressure combination (concurrency cap + cold KV cache) as the root cause.

Immediate actions we're taking now:
- Temporarily increasing your tenant concurrency cap to 24 (30–60 minute window) to relieve queueing.
- Reducing batching window for your traffic to prioritize latency.
- Routing a subset of traffic to an alternate model variant to warm caches.

Expect a noticeable improvement within 5–10 minutes; I'll keep you posted and propose a 11:00 UTC follow-up to verify. Apologies — we're treating this as high priority.

Olga
